analysis.title: Aptiv Plc (APTV): 2027 preliminary guidance below the Street with headwinds from market factors and program roll-offs, but growth in non-auto markets is solid; 3Q26 wrap
key_insights: Aptiv reported 3Q26 revenue of $3,199 mn and adjusted EPS of $1.42, above the Street at $3,167 mn and $1.33. Adjusted EBITDA was $567 mn (17.7% of revenue) vs the Street at $560 mn.

Aptiv gave a preliminary 2027 revenue range of $13.2-13.5 bn and adjusted EBITDA margin of 17.2%-17.5%, implying adjusted EBITDA of $2,270 mn-$2,365 mn. This compares to the Street at $13,206 mn revenue, 19.2% margin and $2,644 mn EBITDA, and GS prior at $12,968 mn, 18.7% and $2,429 mn.

The 2027 outlook assumes weighted global production down 2% at the low end and about flat at the high end, $700 mn of cost inflation recoveries tied to semis (mostly memory), and a $300 mn headwind from net program roll-offs and lower EU-to-China exports. It also assumes 1 point of adjusted EBITDA margin dilution from material inflation pass-throughs. Management said the guidance includes an element of incremental conservatism.
4Q26 guidance is below the Street: revenue $3,110-3,210 mn vs Street $3,192 mn, adjusted EBITDA $582-642 mn vs Street $627 mn, and operating EPS $1.35-$1.55 vs Street $1.62.

2026 guidance midpoint was maintained: revenue $12.65-12.75 bn, adjusted EBITDA $2,310-2,370 mn, operating EPS $5.60-$5.80. The revenue range was narrowed from $12.6-12.8 bn and the FCF guide was narrowed to $625-675 mn from $625-725 mn.

Non-auto revenue grew 11% yoy organically in 3Q. Aptiv is on track for more than $3 bn of non-auto revenue in 2026, up from about $2.9 bn in 2025. Non-auto is about a quarter of revenue. Auto organic revenue fell 1% yoy, in line with customer-weighted vehicle production.
China: YTD China bookings grew 30%, of which more than 20% are tied to export programs. About 10% of revenue is on export platforms and management expects this to reach the mid-teens percent in 2027.
Headwind from two German luxury OEMs is about $250-$300 mn, roughly one third from softer export schedules from Europe to China and the balance from program changeovers.
Capital allocation: at least $650 mn of buybacks planned in 2026 (about $560 mn YTD, $233 mn in 3Q) and 100% of FCF to buybacks in 2027. A portfolio review update is planned for 1Q27.
FY bookings are on track for about $20 bn, but 4Q bookings could be pushed out due to negotiations on commercial recoveries. 3Q bookings were about $4 bn and YTD bookings exceed $13 bn.

GS cut CY26/27/28 EPS to $6.27/$5.95/$7.00 from $6.25/$6.35/$7.25. The 12-month price target fell to $54 from $61, based on 8x (from 9x) normalized EPS of $6.70. Rating stays Buy with 22.1% upside from $44.23.

market_movers.rationale: Target cut to $54 from $61 on a lower multiple of 8x (from 9x) applied to normalized EPS of $6.70. GS sees underlying strength in non-auto and China exports not reflected in valuation.

earnings_insights: 3Q26 reported (11/3): revenue $3,199 mn vs Street (FactSet) $3,167 mn and GS $3,170 mn. Adjusted EBITDA $567 mn (17.7% margin) vs Street $560 mn. Operating (non-GAAP) EPS $1.42 vs Street $1.33, GS $1.32, and guidance of $1.25-$1.35.

4Q26 guidance: revenue $3,110-3,210 mn, adjusted EBITDA $582-642 mn (19.4% margin at midpoint), operating EPS $1.35-$1.55. Street estimates are $3,192 mn, $627 mn and $1.62. The previously implied 4Q EPS midpoint was $1.84.

2026 guidance (pro forma): revenue $12,650-12,750 mn vs Street $12,703 mn, adjusted EBITDA $2,310-2,370 mn vs Street $2,345 mn, operating EPS $5.60-$5.80 vs Street $5.70. The company says this implies 2% yoy organic growth at the midpoint.
Preliminary 2027 guidance (company, not yet final): revenue $13.2-13.5 bn and adjusted EBITDA margin 17.2%-17.5%. Street estimates (consensus, pre-guide) were $13,206 mn, 19.2% and $2,644 mn.
risk_factors: Revenue growth in both auto and non-auto markets.
Possible push-out of 4Q bookings due to negotiations on commercial recoveries.
geopolitical: Softer export volumes from Europe to China for two German luxury OEMs are cited as part of a $250-$300 mn headwind.

tension_points.bull_case: GS sees momentum in engineered components (A&D, industrial/robotics), non-auto at about a quarter of revenue and growing, China export bookings above 20% of YTD bookings, and 100% of FCF going to buybacks in 2027. Management says the 2027 guide embeds extra conservatism and a portfolio review update is due in 1Q27.
tension_points.bear_case: Preliminary 2027 adjusted EBITDA of $2,270-2,365 mn is below the Street at $2,644 mn. Headwinds include flat to down 2% global production, $300 mn of program roll-off and export losses, 1 point of margin dilution from inflation pass-throughs, and 4Q26 guidance below the Street.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A weaker-than-guided 2027 outlook after the 1Q27 portfolio review, or a push-out of 4Q bookings tied to commercial recovery negotiations.

theme_stances.key_argument: Below-Street 2027 EBITDA guidance embeds conservatism, and non-auto and China export strength are not reflected in the current valuation.
theme_stances.evidence: pockets of underlying strength/improvement that we don't think are reflected in the current valuation
